title: Does Explanation Correctness Matter? Linking Computational XAI Evaluation to Human Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2603.25251v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) methods are commonly evaluated using functional correctness metrics, also called faithfulness or fidelity, which estimate how closely an explanation reflects the model's reasoning. Higher correctness is assumed to produce better human understanding, but this link has not been tested with controlled levels. We conducted a user study (N=200) that manipulated explanation correctness at four levels (100%, 85%, 70%, 55%) in a synthetic time series classification task where participants could not rely on domain knowledge or visual intuition. Explanations were constructed to resemble feature attributions, with correctness defined against a known ground truth rather than estimated from a trained model. Participants predicted a simulated AI's decisions from these explanations (forward simulation), and we used their forward simulation accuracy as a proxy for understanding. translated_title: 解释的正确性重要吗？将计算化XAI评估与人类理解联系起来
translated_abstract: 解释性人工智能（XAI）方法通常使用功能正确性指标（也称为忠实度或保真度）进行评估，这些指标衡量解释在多大程度上反映模型的真实推理过程。人们通常假设正确性越高，人类理解效果就越好，但这一联系尚未在受控的正确性水平下得到检验。我们开展了一项用户研究（N=200），在一个合成时间序列分类任务中，将解释正确性操纵在四个水平（100%、85%、70%、55%），参与者无法依赖领域知识或视觉直觉进行判断。解释被构建为类似特征归因的形式，其正确性基于已知的真实标准定义，而非从训练好的模型中估计得出。参与者需要根据这些解释预测模拟AI的决策（前向模拟），我们以其前向模拟准确率作为理解程度的代理指标。正确性影响了前向模拟准确率
tldr: 该研究通过200人用户实验，在四个受控正确性水平（100%、85%、70%、55%）下首次实证检验了解释正确性与人类理解之间的联系，发现解释的功能正确性确实会影响人类对AI决策的前向模拟准确率，从而为计算化XAI评估指标与人类理解之间建立了关联。
en_tdlr: This study empirically links computational XAI evaluation to human understanding through a controlled user study (N=200) manipulating explanation correctness at four levels, demonstrating that functional correctness of explanations significantly affects human forward simulation accuracy.
